about: a visual trend: AI-made clips of one game inside another
lines: Skateboarding, in Call of Duty. Minecraft, in Elden Ring. Tarkov, in Skyrim.
None of these games exist. An AI built them, in hours. And this one just hit twenty-two million views.
The guy who made it says it even runs on a Mac.
Now gamers are at war over it. Genius, or slop? Hold your vote.
Here's the trick. You hand an AI coding model a game, reports name Claude, and say: put this one, inside that one. Hours later, you've got a clip.
Then it became a race. Skate three, inside Modern Warfare two, inside Minecraft. Someone even mashed eight games into one.
Then a Kotaku writer actually played one. Minecraft, inside Skyrim. Missing blocks. Invisible walls. A metal gate that drops wood.
Her verdict: a sandbox built to make viral clips. And she asked what nobody posting these wants to hear. Does anyone actually want to play them?
So what is it? The future of modding, or thirty seconds of slop? Comment one word. Cool, or slop.

about: a money dispute between an esports club's boss and its players' agent
lines: This team packs arenas with tens of thousands of fans. Now its two star players are owed over three hundred thousand euros. That's their own agent talking.
The club is Karmine Corp. Monday night, on stream, co-founder Kameto admitted payments were missed. But he said it's settled, and that the club just cleared five million euros of debt.
Same night, a rival went live. Gotaga, co-founder of Gentle Mates, said the unpaid bill is over three hundred thousand.
Then the players' agent posted this. Several hundred thousand euros, still unpaid. No concrete plan to fix it. And not bonuses. Wages.
The players are Vatira and Atow, two of Rocket League's biggest names. Their contracts end in January.
Kameto says he offered twenty-three thousand euros a month, each. Gentle Mates reportedly offered around twenty-eight.
And the agent says payment problems were the main subject of the talks to stay.
So who do you believe? The boss, who says it's paid? Or the agent, who says it's not? Comment one word. Boss, or agent.

about: a game studio admits it copied an artist's design
lines: This ship can cost seven hundred dollars in a video game. One problem. An artist designed it twelve years ago. And nobody asked.
The game is Modern Warships, published by Gaijin, the company behind War Thunder. The artist is Alex Jay Brady, who posted this design back in twenty-fourteen.
Now look at both. Same deck. Same engines. Same swing wings.
And here's the giveaway. Brady says the original had mistakes. Engines blasting across the deck. Planes taking off backward. The game cloned every one.
Brady's post wasn't even angry. She's looking great. If they'd just asked, and sent some money, zero issue.
Meanwhile, the price. I G N's math: fifty to a hundred dollars in gacha spins. Or up to seven hundred to buy it outright.
Then the studio replied, in public. Fair call. Your design was used as a reference, without proper clearance. We'll make this right.
So is sorry enough? Or should the artist get a cut of every sale? Comment one. Sorry, or pay up.
